messages:
jordan: FYI escalated from ACME netops — calls from their VPC to our private endpoint fail when traffic passes through their re-encrypting proxy (they call it 'edge-reencrypt'). Started after their ADC firmware update. Error seen on client: TLS handshake failure, no HTTP body.

rachel: thanks for the heads up. Do we have any logs or a repro?

jordan: customer sent curl + verbose output and a PCAP. Short snippet from their curl: 

```
$ curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://private.redwood.internal/api/health
* TLSv1.3 (INTERNAL), TLS alert, handshake failure (40):
* stopped the pause stream!
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

Also their edge logs show: `received ClientHello -> sent alert decode_error` (no further detail). They ran `openssl s_client` and got `no peer certificate`.

mike: can you grab the ClientHello bytes? If not, ask them to run: 

```
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -tlsextdebug -status -msg
```

We want to see the extension list and whether GREASE or unusual padding/ordering appears.

anya: @jordan good call. This smells like an extension-order / GREASE handling bug on re-encrypting appliances. Some older TLS stacks (and a couple of ADCs) will reject TLS1.3 ClientHellos that contain GREASE or unusual extension ordering even though that's not kosher. Two quick checks: 1) does forcing TLS1.2 make it work? 2) does disabling TLS1.3 on the proxy (or enabling TLS passthrough) change behavior?

jordan: customer ran tests: forcing TLS1.2 from client works and request succeeds. Forcing TLS1.3 fails. They tried toggling SNI padding on the proxy with no luck.

mike: if TLS1.2 works, that narrows it to TLS1.3 ClientHello differences. Ask them to capture a pcap and run `tshark -r capture.pcap -Y ssl.handshake.type==1 -V` and share the ClientHello section. Also capture `ssldump -A -kr capture.pcap` to show extensions.

jordan: pasted their ClientHello excerpt (sanitized): 

```
ClientHello:
 - legacy_version: 0x0303
 - cipher_suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
 - extensions: supported_versions, supported_groups, signature_algorithms, key_share, psk_key_exchange_modes, psk, application_layer_protocol_negotiation, server_name, padding, GREASE(0x0a0a)
```

anya: yep — GREASE and padding present. Some re-encrypting proxies still run buggy TLS stacks that choke on GREASE or arbitrary extension order. Two remediation paths: 
1) Vendor/firmware upgrade on the proxy (recommended) — file TAC with vendor and point them to TLS1.3 GREASE compatibility notes.
2) Temporary workaround — configure the proxy to pass-through TLS (no re-encrypt) for traffic to our Private endpoint, or limit the proxy to negotiate TLS1.2 for that upstream.

mike: additional short-term customer-side mitigation: if their client can be configured, they can disable GREASE or restrict TLS1.3 ciphers, but that's brittle. Better to treat this as an appliance bug.

jordan: customer is pushing for a targeted workaround they can flip today (they control the ADC). They asked for a specific config snippet for HAProxy / F5 to force TLS1.2 upstream or do passthrough.

anya: suggested example for HAProxy (frontend terminates, backend re-encrypt): 

```
backend redwood_private
  server r1 private.redwood.internal:443 check ssl verify required ssl-min-ver TLSv1.2
  # force TLSv1.2 on backend connection to avoid TLS1.3 ClientHello quirks
```

For F5-ish boxes customers should set "TLS 1.2 only" for the server-side profile or enable TCP pass-through for that pool. Include vendor TAC if they need to keep decrypt/inspect on that path.

rachel: safety note — if they switch to pass-through we lose per-request observability for that traffic; flag for support team and customer success.

jordan: yup noted — CC'ing customer success to manage expectations. I've asked customer to open a TAC with their ADC vendor and to try a backend TLS1.2 limit as a quick test. I also asked for the full pcap and s_client output.

mike: followups from our side: 1) add a KB article template for "re-encrypting proxy rejects TLS1.3 ClientHello / GREASE" with repro steps and suggested workarounds; 2) add a telemetry flag in Private to log ClientHello extension lists (opt-in) so we can triage faster next time.

anya: +1 on the KB. Also include a short troubleshooting checklist: check TLS version, collect ClientHello, try TLS1.2, try passthrough, vendor firmware upgrade.

jordan: customer will try the HAProxy tweak and report back. Marking this thread as open until TAC ticket number comes in. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created ticket #SUP-11458 and linked thread.
